Name: Laura Jones
Badge: Teacher as Researcher: Cultivating Literacy Routines
Looking back on this inquiry cycle, what did you learn about your teaching and your students that you might not have noticed otherwise? How did engaging in this teacher-research process shape or shift your thinking about your classroom practice?:

After this cycle, I learned that a lot of the times, I am feeding things to my students instead of letting them explore and learn it on their own, with corrections from me. This definitely helped me get the idea that I needed to take a step back and let them take ownership of their learning, with guidance from the modules and with finding the connections they need for their individual lives.

Share one artifact or anecdote from trying out your chosen strategy (e.g., a piece of student work, notes from your Writer’s Notebook, a classroom snapshot, or a brief story from the experience).:
What new questions or next steps are you leaving this module with? How might you continue to explore or build on this inquiry in your future teaching?:

I know I want to try using the other strategies later on in my school year, further creating connections and depth to my students learning. I want to make sure that my students understand that what happens in the classroom is not confined to the classroom, and that they can use these strategies and ideas in their lives, not just in their school.
